subject: medicine
title: Large and medium vessel vasculitis: GCA, Takayasu, PAN and Kawasaki

steps.tx: Ask an older adult about **jaw claudication** when chewing, new temporal headache, **scalp tenderness** when combing, and brief visual loss or double vision, since these features suggest giant cell arteritis and threaten blindness. Ask younger patients about **limb claudication** on exertion, absent pulses, neck bruits, and differing pressures between arms, which favour Takayasu arteritis with large vessel narrowing. Tender nodules with livedo rash suggest polyarteritis nodosa. Prolonged fever with strawberry tongue, red eyes, swollen glands, and BCG scar flare suggests Kawasaki disease in children, while tuberculosis can mimic aortitis.
steps.say: Jaw pain on chewing is a classic warning of giant cell arteritis in older adults. New headache with a tender scalp is another feature that is never ignored in clinic. Limb tiredness on exertion with weak pulses is typical of Takayasu disease in young patients. Fever lasting many days with rash and red eyes is suggestive of Kawasaki disease in children.

steps.tx: Palpate the **temporal artery** for beading, tenderness, reduced pulse, and pain when combing the scalp, and test visual fields with acuity plus jaw movement, since giant cell arteritis threatens sight. Compare pulses in all limbs, listen for bruits over neck and abdomen, and record **limb pressures** in both arms, because gaps suggest Takayasu stenoses. Inspect skin for tender nodules, livedo rash, and ulcers of polyarteritis nodosa. Note **strawberry tongue**, red eyes, peeling skin, and cervical glands in Kawasaki disease, and listen to the heart for murmurs of coronary aneurysm.
steps.say: The temporal artery is often tender and beaded when giant cell arteritis is active. Vision is tested with a chart because sudden blindness is the most feared complication. Pulses are compared in every limb while bruits are sought and pressures are recorded. Strawberry tongue with red eyes and swollen glands is characteristic of Kawasaki disease in children.

steps.tx: Study the four panels which show the **temporal artery** swollen in giant cell disease, narrowed aortic branches in Takayasu disease, **beaded aneurysms** of mesenteric vessels in polyarteritis nodosa, and a swollen coronary vessel in Kawasaki disease. The image is useful because each pattern is characteristic and helps fix the disease to its vessel territory for the examination. Recall which lesion threatens sight, which starves limbs of pulses, which bleeds from gut aneurysms, and which scars the heart, then link each panel to its treatment.
steps.say: This image is valuable because four diseases are compared side by side. The swollen temporal artery is shown because threatened sight is the key emergency. Narrowed aortic branches are shown because absent pulses are typical of Takayasu disease. Beaded gut aneurysms are shown because rupture is the feared complication here. The coronary swelling is highlighted because the heart is threatened in Kawasaki disease.

steps.tx: Arrange **artery biopsy** of the temporal vessel to confirm giant cell arteritis, remembering that skip lesions can hide disease and require an adequate sample. Use the **halo sign** on temporal ultrasound as supportive evidence when biopsy is delayed. Request **aortic imaging** by angiography to reveal stenoses and aneurysms of Takayasu arteritis, and link polyarteritis nodosa with hepatitis B aneurysm strings. Check ESR and C reactive protein for activity, exclude tuberculosis with Quantiferon testing, watch coronaries by echo in Kawasaki disease, and separate atherosclerosis, fibromuscular dysplasia, infection, and amyloid mimics.
steps.say: Biopsy of the temporal artery is the standard test that confirms giant cell arteritis. Ultrasound halo around the vessel is supportive evidence while biopsy is awaited. Angiography of the aorta is essential because stenoses are typical of Takayasu disease. Echo of the heart is repeated in Kawasaki disease because aneurysms may develop silently. Blood markers of inflammation are tracked because treatment is guided by their fall.

steps.tx: Give **urgent steroids** when giant cell arteritis threatens vision, since delay risks permanent blindness, and add **tocilizumab** for relapsing disease to spare prolonged steroid harm. Treat Takayasu arteritis with steroids plus mycophenolate and revascularise stenoses by bypass or stenting. Treat polyarteritis nodosa linked to hepatitis B with antivirals plus immunosuppression, and manage Kawasaki disease with **pooled immunoglobulin** timed with echo checks plus **aspirin** for protection. Use killed vaccines, watch vision and pulses and coronaries in follow up, and guard against missed blindness, missed coronary aneurysm, and aneurysm rupture.
steps.say: Steroids are started immediately because threatened vision is never left untreated. Tocilizumab is added in relapse because prolonged steroids are harmful in older patients. Immunoglobulin is given in Kawasaki disease because coronary aneurysms are a feared outcome. Aspirin is used for protection while the coronary arteries are watched by echo. Vision and pulses are reviewed at follow up because late relapse is always possible.
